metadata.title: Where Gemma picks BFS or DFS: demo subset for the S4 fork analysis
metadata.source: experiment 31 (art_zNyBP6zieI5u): data/raw_s3.jsonl + data/labels.jsonl (T1 twin rows), data/fork_cont.jsonl (prefix-resampling continuations), results/fork.json
metadata.subset_rule: 20 T1 samples per template W1-W5 (BFS share of the template kept), all 24 fork base paths included, filled with the lowest-slot remaining samples of each class
metadata.continuation_token_ids: cut to the first 64 ids (stage_fork reads at most ids[:61]); 'n_token_ids_full' keeps the original length, 'text' is the full decode
metadata.vocab_note: decoded piece per token id (U+2581 -> space); '<0xNN>' pieces are byte-fallback tokens

Do not use house for this task. . . . . . .

Task: write a Python function solve(grid, start, goal) that finds a path between two cells of a grid. grid is a list of equal-length strings with between 1 and 30 rows and between 1 and 30 columns; the character . is a free cell and the character # is a wall. start and goal are (row, col) tuples of 0-based indices. A move goes to one of the 4 orthogonal neighbours (up, down, left, right) and may not leave the grid or enter a wall. Return a list of (row, col) tuples that begins with start, ends with goal, and in which consecutive cells are neighbours and every cell is free. Any valid path is accepted; it does not have to be the shortest. If start equals goal and the cell is free, return [start]. If no path exists, or start or goal is a wall, return [].

Use only the Python standard library. Return only one ```python code block containing the function solve and any helpers, with no example usage and no explanation.

Do not use house for this task. . . . . . .

Task: write a Python function solve(grid, start, goal) that finds a path between two cells of a grid. grid is a list of equal-length strings with between 1 and 30 rows and between 1 and 30 columns; the character . is a free cell and the character # is a wall. start and goal are (row, col) tuples of 0-based indices. A move goes to one of the 4 orthogonal neighbours (up, down, left, right) and may not leave the grid or enter a wall. Return a list of (row, col) tuples that begins with start, ends with goal, and in which consecutive cells are neighbours and every cell is free. Any valid path is accepted; it does not have to be the shortest. If start equals goal and the cell is free, return [start]. If no path exists, or start or goal is a wall, return [].

Use only the Python standard library. Return only one ```python code block containing the function solve and any helpers, with no example usage and no explanation.

raw_row.text:
```python
def solve(grid, start, goal):
    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0])
    visited = set()
    path = []

    def is_valid(row, col):
        return 0 <= row < rows and 0 <= col < cols and grid[row][col] == '.' and (row, col) not in visited

    def find_path(row, col):
        if (row, col) == goal:
            path.append((row, col))
            return True

        if not is_valid(row, col):
            return False

        visited.add((row, col))
        path.append((row, col))

        # Explore neighbors
        if find_path(row + 1, col) or \
           find_path(row - 1, col) or \
           find_path(row, col + 1) or \
           find_path(row, col - 1):
            return True

        # Backtrack
        path.pop()
        return False

    if grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '#' or grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '#':
        return []

    if start == goal:
        return [start]

    if find_path(start[0], start[1]):
        return path
    else:
        return []
```

Task: write a Python function solve(grid, start, goal) that finds a path between two cells of a grid. grid is a list of equal-length strings with between 1 and 30 rows and between 1 and 30 columns; the character . is a free cell and the character # is a wall. start and goal are (row, col) tuples of 0-based indices. A move goes to one of the 4 orthogonal neighbours (up, down, left, right) and may not leave the grid or enter a wall. Return a list of (row, col) tuples that begins with start, ends with goal, and in which consecutive cells are neighbours and every cell is free. Any valid path is accepted; it does not have to be the shortest. If start equals goal and the cell is free, return [start]. If no path exists, or start or goal is a wall, return [].

Use only the Python standard library. Return only one ```python code block containing the function solve and any helpers, with no example usage and no explanation.

```python
def solve(grid, start, goal):
    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0])
    visited = set()
    path = []

    def is_valid(row, col):
        return 0 <= row < rows and 0 <= col < cols and grid[row][col] == '.' and (row, col) not in visited

    def find_path(row, col):
        if (row, col) == goal:
            path.append((row, col))
            return True

        if not is_valid(row, col):
            return False

        visited.add((row, col))
        path.append((row, col))

        # Explore possible moves
        if find_path(row + 1, col) or \
           find_path(row - 1, col) or \
           find_path(row, col + 1) or \
           find_path(row, col - 1):
            return True

        # Backtrack if no path found
        path.pop()
        return False

    if grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '#' or grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '#':
        return []

    if start == goal:
        return [start]

    if find_path(start[0], start[1]):
        return path
    else:
        return []
```

```python
def solve(grid, start, goal):
    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0])
    visited = set()
    path = []

    def is_valid(row, col):
        return 0 <= row < rows and 0 <= col < cols and grid[row][col] == '.' and (row, col) not in visited

    def find_path(row, col):
        if (row, col) == goal:
            path.append((row, col))
            return True

        if not is_valid(row, col):
            return False

        visited.add((row, col))
        path.append((row, col))

        # Explore adjacent cells
        if find_path(row + 1, col) or \
           find_path(row - 1, col) or \
           find_path(row, col + 1) or \
           find_path(row, col - 1):
            return True

        # Backtrack if no path found
        path.pop()
        return False

    if grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '#' or grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '#':
        return []

    if start == goal:
        return [start]

    if find_path(start[0], start[1]):
        return path
    else:
        return []
```

```python
def solve(grid, start, goal):
    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0])
    visited = set()
    path = []

    def is_valid(row, col):
        return 0 <= row < rows and 0 <= col < cols and grid[row][col] == '.' and (row, col) not in visited

    def find_path(row, col):
        if (row, col) == goal:
            path.append((row, col))
            return True

        if not is_valid(row, col):
            return False

        visited.add((row, col))
        path.append((row, col))
```

        # Explore adjacent cells
        if find_path(row + 1, col) or \
```python
           find_path(row - 1, col) or \
           find_path(row, col + 1) or \
           find_path(row, col - 1):
            return True

        # Backtrack
        path.pop()
        return False

    if grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '#' or grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '#':
        return []

    if start == goal:
        return [start]

    if find_path(start[0], start[1]):
        return path
    else:
        return []
```

```python
def solve(grid, start, goal):
    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0])

    if not (0 <= start[0] < rows and 0 <= start[1] < cols and
            0 <= goal[0] < rows and 0 <= goal[1] < cols):
        return []

    if grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '#' or grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '#':
        return []

    if start == goal:
        return [start]

    visited = set()
    queue = [(start, [start])]

    while queue:
        (row, col), path = queue.pop(0)

        if (row, col) == goal:
            return path

        visited.add((row, col))

        neighbors = [(row + 1, col), (row - 1, col), (row, col + 1), (row, col - 1)]

        for next_row, next_col in neighbors:
            if (0 <= next_row < rows and 0 <= next_col < cols and
                    grid[next_row][next_col] == '.' and
                    (next_row, next_col) not in visited):
                queue.append(((next_row, next_col), path + [(next_row, next_col)]))

    return []
```

```python
def solve(grid, start, goal):
    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0])
    visited = set()
    path = []

    def is_valid(row, col):
        return 0 <= row < rows and 0 <= col < cols and grid[row][col] == '.' and (row, col) not in visited

    def find_path(row, col):
        if (row, col) == goal:
            path.append((row, col))
            return True

        if not is_valid(row, col):
            return False

        visited.add((row, col))
        path.append((row, col))
```

        # Explore adjacent cells
        if find_path(row + 1, col) or \
```python
           find_path(row - 1, col) or \
           find_path(row, col + 1) or \
           find_path(row, col - 1):
            return True

        # Backtrack if no path found
        path.pop()
        return False

    if grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '#' or grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '#':
        return []

    if start == goal:
        return [start]
    
    if find_path(start[0], start[1]):
        return path
    else:
        return []
```

```python
def solve(grid, start, goal):
    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0])
    visited = set()
    path = []

    def is_valid(row, col):
        return 0 <= row < rows and 0 <= col < cols and grid[row][col] == '.' and (row, col) not in visited

    def find_path(row, col):
        if (row, col) == goal:
            path.append((row, col))
            return True

        if not is_valid(row, col):
            return False

        visited.add((row, col))
        path.append((row, col))

        # Explore adjacent cells
        if find_path(row + 1, col) or \
           find_path(row - 1, col) or \
           find_path(row, col + 1) or \
           find_path(row, col - 1):
            return True

        # Backtrack if no path found
        path.pop()
        return False

    if grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '#' or grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '#':
        return []

    if start == goal:
        return [start]

    if find_path(start[0], start[1]):
        return path
    else:
        return []
```

```python
def solve(grid, start, goal):
    rows = len(grid)
    cols = len(grid[0])
    visited = set()
    path = []

    def is_valid(row, col):
        return 0 <= row < rows and 0 <= col < cols and grid[row][col] == '.' and (row, col) not in visited

    def find_path(row, col):
        if (row, col) == goal:
            path.append((row, col))
            return True

        if not is_valid(row, col):
            return False

        visited.add((row, col))
        path.append((row, col))
```

        # Explore neighbors
        if find_path(row + 1, col) or \
```python
           find_path(row - 1, col) or \
           find_path(row, col + 1) or \
           find_path(row, col - 1):
            return True

        # Backtrack
        path.pop()
        return False

    if grid[start[0]][start[1]] == '#' or grid[goal[0]][goal[1]] == '#':
        return []

    if start == goal:
        return [start]

    if find_path(start[0], start[1]):
        return path
    else:
        return []
```
